links.outcome: Participant diagnostic accuracy and precision with versus without BiTNet assistance
links.effect: Mean accuracy and precision with BiTNet (0.74 and 0.61) were statistically higher than without (0.50 and 0.46), p<0.001; improved at all experience levels.
links.quote: The mean accuracy and precision of the participants with BiTNet as an assisting tool (0.74 and 0.61, respectively) are statistically higher than those of participants without the assisting tool (0.50 and 0.46, respectively (p<0.001)).

unlisted_practices: Modifying the model architecture to reduce overconfident prediction probabilities
Using prediction-probability thresholds for auto-prescreening to reduce radiologist workload

links.effect: With BiTNet, mean accuracy/precision were 0.74/0.61 versus 0.50/0.46 without (p<0.001).
links.quote: The mean accuracy and precision of the participants with BiTNet as an assisting tool (0.74 and 0.61, respectively) are statistically higher than those of participants without the assisting tool (0.50 and 0.46, respectively (p<0.001)).

links.effect: With BiTNet, mean accuracy/precision were 0.74/0.61 versus 0.50/0.46 without (p<0.001).

links.effect: Auto-prescreening reduced radiologist workload by 35%, with false negatives as low as 1 out of every 455 images.
links.quote: The proposed BiTNet can reduce the workload of radiologists by 35% while keeping the false negatives to as low as 1 out of every 455 images.

links.effect: No numeric overconfidence metric reported; modifications to EfficientNet solved overconfidence and improved both applications and healthcare professionals.
links.quote: Our experiments suggest that prediction probability has an impact on both applications, and our modifications to EfficientNet solve the overconfidence problem, thereby improving the performance of both applications and of healthcare professionals.
